sentences.text: Eocaiman is an extinct genus of South American alligatorid, a type of crocodile-like reptile. It belongs to the order Crocodilia and the family Alligatoridae, placing it within the subfamily Caimaninae. Its parent group is Globidonta, and it is classified as a reptile within the class Sauropsida.

The genus was named by Simpson in 1933. The first species, Eocaiman cavernensis, was identified from a holotype found in Argentina. A second species, Eocaiman palaeocenicus, was discovered in the Salamanca Formation of Argentina. The third species, Eocaiman itaboraiensis, was found in Brazil. An undescribed species was also found at the La Venta site in Colombia. There are seven recorded fossil occurrences of Eocaiman in total.
The genus Eocaiman is divided into four species, some of which are considered doubtful. The species Notocaiman stromeri was once considered a synonym of Eocaiman.

Eocaiman species lived from the Early Paleocene to the Miocene in what is now Argentina, Brazil, and Colombia. The time range for Eocaiman is from the Danian to the Tortonian, spanning 66 to 11 million years ago.
